statements.subject: server
statements.description: Whenever there is a relevant change to the server state, the results of this command are required to change accordingly.
actions: update CAPABILITIES response to reflect current server state

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Some clients may therefore wish to remember which extensions a server supports to avoid the delay of an additional command and response, particularly if they open multiple connections in the same session.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: However, information about extensions related to security and privacy MUST NOT be cached, since this could allow a variety of attacks.
actions: discard security-related and privacy-related capability information
do not persist security or privacy capability data across sessions

statements.subject: nntp
statements.description: Any security extension should include requirements to check the security state of the link in a manner appropriate to that extension.
actions: verify security state of the link before proceeding with the security extension

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Caching should normally only be considered for anonymous clients that do not use any security or privacy extensions and for which the time required for an additional command and response is a noticeable issue.
